title: Codex Fixes Video Bug in Nearly 20-Year-Old Radeon GPUs
summary: AI-assisted patch brings video playback fixes to legacy AMD Radeon GPUs from 2007. One RV610 chip confirmed working, four more families awaiting tests.
body_markdown:
**Officially launched on November 15, 2026.**


#### 💡 TL;DR


- OpenAI Codex generated a Linux kernel patch fixing video playback on AMD Radeon GPUs from 2007, successfully tested on one RV610 iMac.
- The fix targets five legacy GPU families (RV610, R500, RV515, RV530, RV570) and is queued for Linux kernel version 7.5 release.
- Community testers are needed to verify the patch works across all targeted Radeon hardware before final upstream merge.


A Codex-assisted kernel patch has successfully restored video playback functionality to AMD Radeon graphics cards that first shipped in 2007. The fix, confirmed working on one RV610-based iMac, is now queued for inclusion in Linux kernel 7.5, but maintainers are seeking community testers to validate the patch across four additional legacy GPU families before final merge.


## AI-Generated Fix Targets Five GPU Families


The patch addresses a long-standing video decoding regression affecting five Radeon architectures: RV610, R500, RV515, RV530, and RV570. These chips powered mid-range desktop and mobile systems between 2006 and 2008, representing millions of units still in service on open-source driver stacks. OpenAI's Codex model generated the core driver logic after being prompted with hardware specifications, existing codebase context, and regression reports from users experiencing black screens during video playback.


One developer confirmed successful video rendering on an RV610-equipped iMac after applying the patch locally. The fix modifies power management and memory allocation routines in the Radeon DRM driver, correcting a timing issue introduced in earlier kernel versions when legacy hardware paths were refactored. Testing revealed stable 1080p playback across multiple video codecs with no thermal or stability regressions.


## Community Testing Required Before Upstream Merge


Linux kernel maintainers have flagged the patch for broader community validation before accepting it into the mainline tree. While the RV610 test case demonstrates viability, the other four GPU families (R500, RV515, RV530, RV570) share similar but not identical hardware architectures. Each requires independent verification to ensure the memory timing adjustments do not trigger unexpected behavior on variants with different VRAM configurations or display output topologies.


Testers with compatible hardware are encouraged to apply the patch from the kernel mailing list and report results through standard bug tracking channels. The merge window for Linux 7.5 closes in early December 2026, giving the community approximately three weeks to validate functionality across the target hardware range.


## Release Date


The Codex-generated patch was officially submitted to the Linux kernel mailing list on November 15, 2026, with initial RV610 testing completed the same day. If community validation succeeds, the fix will ship in Linux kernel 7.5, expected to reach stable release in late December 2026 or early January 2027.


## What This Means


This deployment demonstrates how large language models trained on open-source codebases can accelerate maintenance of legacy hardware that commercial vendors have long abandoned. For users running Linux distributions on nearly two-decade-old machines, AI-assisted patches offer a lifeline for continued functionality without requiring deep driver expertise. The success of this fix may encourage broader adoption of LLM-generated patches in niche hardware support scenarios where human developer bandwidth is scarce.
